To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a regulatory gene locus, rlambda1, controls a DNA level event in stem cells which is required for their differentiation into B lymphocytes which express a particular lambda light chain.

(1) the rlambda1 regulatory locus controls the expression of lambda1 light chains; (2) the rlambda 1 regulatory locus is linked to the lambda 1 structural gene; (3) the rlambda locus controls a DNA-level event; (4) the rlambda regulatory locus is a single locus which has a clear gene dosage affect.
a regulatory gene locus controls the expression of the lambda1 light chain and that this regulatory gene locus is located near the lambda1 structural genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic control of the expression of a single immunoglobulin light chain.
the genetic regulation of the expression of the lambda1 light chain in the mouse.
the molecular basis of the immune response.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rlambda 1 gene is a regulatory gene controlling expression of the lambda1 structural genes.
the rlambda + gene locus controls the number of B cells expressing the lambda1 light chain and is not linked to the major histocompatiblity complex (MHC) or to the lambda heavy chain allotype.

the rlambda 1 regulatory gene locus is a regulatory gene locus controlling lambda1 light chain gene expression which is linked to the lambda 1 locus, is not linked to the major histocompatability complex, and is not linked to a heavy chain allotype locus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rlambda 1 regulatory gene locus is a locus which influences a DNA level event which is required for the expression of the lambda1 light chain locus in the mouse.
the rlambda 1 locus is a regulatory locus controlling a DNA level recognition site involved in the transposition of a v-gene into a transcriptional unit with the cl gene.
the expression of the rlambda 1 regulatory gene is necessary for the normal expression of the lambda1 structural locus.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the expression of a single light chain structural gene locus is under the control of at least two regulatory gene loci, one of which, rlambda1, is a locus of major effect and is probably the first of many such regulatory loci to be discovered.

the expression of the lambda1 light chain in mice is under the influence of two separate gene loci, the lambda1 structural locus and the regulatory locus rlambda1, and that the latter locus is involved in a DNA level event occurring during the commitment of stem cells to lambda1 expression.
the expression of a single light chain gene locus can be controlled by at least two distinct gene loci: the structural gene locus itself (lambda1) and a regulatory gene locus (rlambda1).
